text:
alex: Alert from monitoring — dedicated-usw2 pool p99 latency jumped to 1.8s for tenant T-42 and throughput dropped ~30% starting ~10:03 UTC. SLA page shows errors + evictions. Investigating.

mira: seeing same in traces. Lots of KV cache evictions on host-27/host-29. Metrics: `kv.cache_evictions: 118`, `slot_evictions: 42` in 10m window. :eyes:

jamal: any change in kernel selection? profiler shows repeated fallback from `matmul_opt_v3` -> `matmul_ref` on host-29 around the spike.

alex: good catch. Logs: `kernel_select(reason=compatibility_mismatch, model=llama-2-13b, seq=2048) -> matmul_ref` repeated. Putting that in the incident timeline.

sre-oncall: infra-bot pushed a scale plan at 10:05 but it didn't increase usable slots — looks like placement constraints prevented allocations.

infra-bot: [AUTO] attempted pool-scale-up(dedicated-usw2): requested +6 slots, placement failures: affinity_constraint_violation (tenant_tag mismatch)

ryan: aha — tenant T-42 had an incorrect affinity_tag after the recent rollout. Scheduler treats them as low-priority and spreads small slices across many hosts -> noisy neighbor and hot-host concentration. Repro config snippet:
```
placement_policy {
  tenant_id: "T-42"
  affinity_tag: "high-memory"  # expected "compute-intensive"
}
```

mira: that explains the KV churn: prefix caching ineffective when the same tenant gets scheduled across different hosts. Cache hit rate dropped from 86% -> 37% at spike.

sylvia: batching heuristics also changed yesterday — `batching.max_wait_ms` bumped to 2000 in canary which increases queueing and makes some kernels more sensitive. Might amplify p99 when kernel falls back.

jamal: timeline looks like: affinity_tag change (09:58) -> batching tweak rollout (10:00) -> eviction spike + kernel fallbacks (10:03) -> p99 jump (10:05). Multi-factor.

alex: triage plan:
- rollback affinity_tag for T-42 to `compute-intensive`
- rollback batching change in canary -> reduce `max_wait_ms` to 50
- collect `perfkit` traces from host-27/29 (kernels + NVTX)
- increase tenant slot quota temporarily to reduce evictions
- open follow-up to investigate kernel fallback root cause

mira: started rollback affinity at 10:12 (deploy id: rollback-214). Scheduler log shows new allocations consolidating tenant onto proper host pool.

infra-bot: [AUTO] rollout rollback-214 completed at 10:15, allocation delta: consolidated 6 slots into affinity group `compute-intensive`.

ryan: after consolidation, KV hitrate rising back to ~78% and p99 falling to 420ms. Still see intermittent `matmul_ref` fallbacks — need kernel profiling.

jamal: I'm grabbing kernel traces + a short perf recording from host-29. Attaching logs to JIRA: https://jira.internal/redwood/INFR-7219

sre-oncall: temporary mitigation applied: bumped tenant quota by +3 slots to avoid immediate evictions until we confirm kernel patch. :thumbsup:

sylvia: note for postmortem: rollout gating is weak on changes that affect placement-affinity tags. Recommend adding a placement-affinity checklist and e2e sim for batching vs kernel combos.

alex: hitting summary for incident report: root causes are (1) mis-applied affinity tag causing noisy-host spreading and KV cache invalidation, (2) batching heuristic change that increased tail latency when combined with kernel fallbacks, (3) kernel fallback frequency increased under those conditions (investigating whether compilation/kernel selection bug or resource contention). Actions: rollbacks applied, quota bump, kernel traces collected (INFR-7219), follow-up fixes: scheduler validation + batching canary rollback policy + kernel selection sanity tests.

mira: marking as mitigated — continuing to monitor. If p99 creeps back up, we reopen. :white_check_mark:

alex: thanks all. I'll draft the postmortem with timeline + metric graphs next.
